title: Thunder on Sinai (Exodus 19)
hook: smoke, trumpet, trembling mountain, and a people at the foot

segments.voice: Yesterday, Jethro watched Moses judge from sunrise to sunset and told him the truth. Your line was you can't do it alone. What did you hand over? Day three hundred ninety-three.

Three months out of Egypt, the people come to a mountain in the desert and pitch their tents at its foot. They've seen a sea open. They've eaten bread that fell with the dew. And now Moses goes up and comes down, up and down, carrying messages. Wash your clothes, he tells them. Get ready. In three days something is going to happen. Put a boundary around the mountain, and don't touch it. On the morning of the third day, it starts. Thunder. Lightning. A cloud sitting heavy on the peak. And then a sound nobody expects from a mountain: a trumpet, a ram's horn, getting louder and louder. The whole camp trembles.
screen: `THREE MONTHS OUT OF EGYPT.` → `WASH, AND WAIT THREE DAYS.` → `A TRUMPET FROM THE MOUNTAIN.`

segments.voice: The King James Bible tells it like this: "there were thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud upon the mount, and the voice of the trumpet exceeding loud; so that all the people that was in the camp trembled." Then the mountain itself: "mount Sinai was altogether on a smoke, because the LORD descended upon it in fire," and "the whole mount quaked greatly." Smoke like a furnace. A trumpet with no trumpeter. Notice what this scene is for. It isn't a lecture. Before a single law is given, the people are made to feel how big the One speaking is. Awe comes first. But it isn't only terror. Just before the thunder, God sends Moses down with a gentle message: you saw how I carried you on eagles' wings and brought you to myself. And then a promise: you'll be a kingdom of priests, a holy nation. A whole people, not just a few, set apart. So the mountain shakes, and the voice says, I brought you here because I wanted you. Where is Sinai? Honestly, nobody knows for sure. Since the early centuries of the church, Christian tradition has pointed to a granite peak in the south of the Sinai Peninsula, where a monastery has stood since the sixth century. Scholars have proposed other mountains. The Bible sometimes calls it Horeb, and it never pins it to a map. For Christians, this mountain echoes forward. Jewish tradition remembers the giving of the law at the feast of Shavuot. Christians call that same feast Pentecost, and in the book of Acts it's the day the Spirit came with wind and fire.
screen: `THUNDER, CLOUD, TRUMPET, SMOKE.` · `AWE COMES BEFORE THE LAW.` · `ON EAGLES' WINGS, TO MYSELF.` · `NOBODY KNOWS WHERE IT IS.` · then, large: `THE WHOLE MOUNT QUAKED GREATLY.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: feel awe at something vast. Settle, and breathe. Picture the biggest thing you've ever stood near. A mountain range. The ocean at night. A thunderstorm rolling in. A sky so full of stars it made you dizzy. Put yourself back at its foot. Notice how small you felt, and that small didn't feel bad, exactly. It felt like the right size. Stay there. If you pray, you can simply stand before God in that smallness, without words. If you don't, let the vastness be enough. The bell holds the time.
Sinai. The mountain in the desert where the people camped three months after Egypt, wrapped in smoke and thunder, where the law was given.
Your line: the mountain shook. Today, when you see something bigger than you, a storm, a skyline, a tree, stop for five seconds and let it be big. Day three hundred ninety-three.

screen: `DAY 393 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE TEN WORDS, PART ONE.`

howItsDone: Christians read Exodus 19 as the prelude to the Ten Commandments, and some churches read it around Pentecost, which falls on the Jewish feast of Shavuot, remembered in Jewish tradition as the time the law was given at Sinai.

fork.setup: you're camped at the foot of the mountain. it's smoking, the ground is shaking, and a trumpet is blaring with no one blowing it. what do you do?
options: climb up for a closer look.
stay at the boundary, and tremble.
pack up and head back to Egypt.
fork.reveal: the people stay at the foot and tremble. the boundary was there on purpose: the scene is built to make them feel how great the One speaking is.

original.note: Hebrew: the mountain's name. Its meaning and its place on the map are both uncertain.

trapdoor: what you thought: a mountain where Moses got the rules.
what it means: a meeting. thunder and smoke make the people feel God's greatness, and the voice says, I brought you here to myself.
what a scholar hears: Sinai, also called Horeb. tradition points to one peak in the south of the peninsula, but the Bible never fixes it on a map.

notes: 'Three months out of Egypt' from Exodus 19:1 ('in the third month'); confirm.

Traditional site: Jebel Musa, with St. Catherine's Monastery (built under Justinian, sixth century); 'since the early centuries of the church' refers to fourth-century pilgrim tradition (e.g., Egeria). Confirm wording.
Pentecost/Shavuot: the identification of Shavuot with the giving of the law is rabbinic tradition, not stated in Exodus; the script says 'Jewish tradition remembers'. Confirm.

Original: the meaning of the name Sinai is uncertain (some link it to the moon god Sin, or to seneh, 'bush'); the note says only that it is uncertain. Transliteration 'see-NIGH' reflects the Hebrew Sinai; confirm.
